sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 and requested this Court to set aside the Arbitral Award dated 04.02.2020 passed in case No.LAQ/ARB/NH- 7/134/2012-13 pertaining to Sy.No. 29/2 by respondent No.2 A.P. No.35/2020 .2.
In the petition it is stated that National Highways Authority of India was constituted by an Act of the Parliament, "the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988" .

entities.text: National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of National Highways entrusted to it and for matters connected thereto.

.3. It is stated that the Central Government for the purpose of widening / upgradation maintenance,
management and operation of NH-7 on the stretch of land from kms. 526.50 to kms. 535 & Kms.
539 to Kms 556 of Hyderabad - Bengaluru Section issued preliminary notification dated 05.12.2002 under Section 3-A(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 in-respect of acquisition of lands situated at Kadiganahalli village, Bengaluru North Taluka.
The preliminary notification was published on 23.12.2002.

The final notification was published in the official Gazette on 22.07.2003.
.4.

It is stated that under the said notification for the 1st stage of acquisition non-agricultural lands in Sy.No. 29/2 to an extent of 2904 sq. feet, situated at the A.P. No.35/2020 said village belonging to the respondent No. 1 were also acquired.
.5.
It is stated that the respondent No.3 vide award dated 08.03.2004 determined the market value of NA lands at Rs.45/- per sq. feet.
The respondent No. 3 observed that the average of the sale statistics of NA lands was Rs. 46/- per sq. feet and the guidance value was Rs. 45/- per sq. feet.

Since both the average of the sales statistics as well as the guidance value were on almost the same, the respondent No. 3 examined the physical characteristics of the acquired lands, relied upon the guidance value and determined the market value of NA lands at Rs. 45/- per sq. feet.
.6. It is stated that a sum of Rs. 1,30,680/- was disbursed as compensation to the respondent No.1 towards the subject lands.
Being dissatisfied with the amount awarded by the respondent No.3 the respondent No.1 belatedly approached the respondent No.2 under Section 3-G (5) of the NH Act.

It A.P./35/2020 on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168729828/
2 is stated that the petitioner entered appearance and filed its A.P. No.35/2020 statement of objections with documents in support of his defence.

The respondent No.2 without application of mind and proper appreciation of facts, passed an arbitral award and redetermined the market value at Rs.125/- per sq. feet for the subject lands acquired from respondent No.1.

(c) The respondent No. 2 has not complied with the provision of Section 28 of the A &
C Act, while passing the impugned award and therefore, it is patently illegal and requires to be set aside.

A.P. No.35/2020 (d) Both the sale statistics and guidance values were on the same side which clearly establishes that the basis for arriving at the market value of Rs. 45/- per sq. feet was sound and in accordance with Section 3-G(7)
(a) of the NH Act.
This aspect of the matter has not at all been taken into account or cited by the respondent No. 2 at page 8 of the impugned Arbitral Award.
(e) the respondent No. 2 has relied upon a notification, which came into effect after the publication of preliminary notification, the impugned award is opposed to Section 3- G(7)(a) of the NH Act.
(f) The respondent No. 2 has also failed to follow the procedure laid down in Section 24 of the A & C Act.

(g) The respondent No. 2 has given the benefit of enhancement to the respondent No. 1 without production by the respondent No. 1 of any records or evidence in support of such enhancement which is completely arbitrary.
(h) The impugned Arbitral Award is not a speaking order and liable to be set aside.
Heard the arguments.

.8. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
A.P./35/2020 on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168729828/
3
(1) Whether the petitioner proves any of the grounds mentioned under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, to set aside the award passed by the learned Arbitrator?
(2) What order or award?

.9. My findings on the above points are:
Point No.1 : In the affirmative, Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .10. POINT No.1: Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996 provide the circumstances under which an award can be set aside by a Civil Court.
It provides that- 1) if a party was under some incapacity; or 2) that the arbitration agreement is not valid under any law which the parties are subjected to ; or A.P. No.35/2020 3) the party was not given proper notice of the appointment of the arbitrator or arbitral proceedings; or 4) that the award is not within the terms of the arbitration agreement; or 5) the composition of arbitral tribunal or the arbitral procedure is not accordance with the agreement of parties;
6) The subject matter of the dispute is not capable of settlement by Arbitrator under the law for the time being in force;
7) that the arbitral award is in conflict with the pubic policy of India etc., Explanation shows (1) that an award is in conflict with the pubic policy of India if the making of the award was induced or affected by fraud or corruption or was in violation of Section 75 or Section 81.
(2) It is in conflict with contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian Law or iii) It is in conflict with most basic notion of morality or justice.
Explanation 2. The test as to whether there is contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian law shall not entail a review on the merits of the dispute.

It may also be set aside if the Court finds the award is vitiated by patent illegality appearing on the face of award provided that an award shall not be set aside merely on the A.P./35/2020 on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168729828/
4 ground of an erroneous application of law or by re appreciation of evidence.

.11. In Kwality Manufacturing Corporation Vs. Central Whorehouse Corporation (2009) 5 Sec.142, it has been held that:
"From a catena of other judgments of this Court, it is clear that for the objector /
appellant in order to succeed in their challenge against an arbitral award, they must show that the award of the Arbitrator suffered from perversity or an error of law or that the Arbitrator has otherwise misconducted himself.

entities.text: Kwality Manufacturing Corporation Vs. Central Whorehouse Corporation (2009) 5 Sec.142
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Merely showing that there is another reasonable interpretation or possible view on the basis of the material on the record is insufficient to allow for the interference by the Court."
Bearing in mind the above section and decision, now it has to be seen whether the impugned award suffers from any patent error, illegality as envisaged above.
The petitioner has stated that the award was passed by the respondent No.3 - L.A.O. on 08.03.2004.
The respondent No. 1 approached the respondent No. 2 seeking enhancement of compensation only during 2012 i.e., almost after a lapse of 8 years from the date of passing of the award.
It is contended that the respondent No. 2 had failed to note the claim of respondent No. 1 was barred by time.

.13. In support of his contention, the petitioner counsel has relied upon the decision reported in (2016) 14 SCC 761 (State of Gujarath Vs. Kothari and Associates), wherein it has been held that:
" A. Limitation Act, 1963 - S. e - Issue of limitation - Duty of trial Court to consider, if said issue is not raised by parties concerned- Failure of trial Court to consider the issue in such a case - Effect of - Right to raise the issue in appeal. - Held, it is incumbent upon Trial Court to consider the issue of limitation on its own initiative even if that issue is not raised by parties concerned-

entities.text: (2016) 14 SCC 761 (State of Gujarath Vs. Kothari and Associates)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where the issue of limitation was not raised during trial by appellant State and also the trial Court failed to consider that issue on its own initiative, held, the said issue could be A.P. No.35/2020 raised in appeal including any successive appeal."
The above decision applies to the case on hand.
.14. The preliminary notification in the present case was issued on 05.12.2002.
The award has been passed on 08.03.2004.
The compensation has been received by the respondent No. 1 on 26.05.2012.
The application before the Arbitrator has been filed on 25.08.2012.

In-spite of taking specific contention with regard to limitation by the petitioner, the respondent No. 1 did not choose to appear and give explanation with regard to delay in approaching the respondent No. 2 Arbitrator.

.15. As per Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act which reads as under:
"3G(5) - If the amount determined by the competent authority under Sub Section (1)
or Sub Section (2) is not acceptable to either of the parties, the amount shall, on an A.P./35/2020 on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168729828/
5 application by either of the parties, be determined by the Arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government."

In W.A. No. 31066/2012 & 31094-96/2012 (T. Yunis Vs. National Highways Authority of India and others), wherein our Hon'ble High Court has held that:
"No period of limitation has been stipulated to seek a reference under Section 3G(5)
of the National Highways Act.

entities.text: W.A. No. 31066/2012 & 31094-96/2012 (T. Yunis Vs. National Highways Authority of India and others)
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: In such circumstances, the only provision available to the parties is to invoke Article 137 of the Limitation Act, which provides three years from the date on which right to apply accrues".
The said decision applies to the case on hand.
As per the said decision within a period of 3 years from the date of passing of award right to file application before the Arbitrator arises.
The award has been passed on 08.03.2004.
The respondent No.1 ought to have filed the application before the Arbitrator on or before 08.03.2007.

As the application is filed on 25.08.2012 before the Arbitrator,
application was barred by limitation.
.17.
The Arbitrator has stated that the LAO has informed that the application can be filed within 3 years from the date of receipt of compensation and so the A.P. No.35/2020 application is in time.
The compensation amount is received by the respondent No.1 on 26.05.2012, even though the award has been passed on 08.03.2004.
The claimant has not explained the delay in filing the application.
The application filed before the Arbitrator is beyond 3 years and so the proceedings before the Arbitrator was barred by limitation.
.18. The petitioner has contended that Arbitrator has relied upon the guidance value for year 2005-06 published on 07.10.2005.
Preliminary notification in the present case was issued on 05.12.2002.

The petitioner has contended that the respondent No. 2 has relied upon the notification, which came to effect after publication of preliminary notification, the impugned award is opposed to Section 3-G(7)(a) of the NH Act.

.19. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd., Vs. SAW Pipes Ltd. (AIR 2003 SC 2629) has held that:
 "if the award is contrary to the  Substantive provisions of law or the  A.P. No.35/2020 provisions of the Act or against the terms of the contract, it would be patently illegal, which could be interfered under Section 34".

entities.text: Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd., Vs. SAW Pipes Ltd. (AIR 2003 SC 2629)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The above decision applies to the case on hand.
The Arbitrator relying upon the guidelines value dated 07.10.2005 has enhanced the market value from Rs. 45/- per sq. feet to 125/- per sq. feet without assigned any reason.

Even if the Arbitrator had relied upon the said notification, he ought to A.P./35/2020 on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168729828/
6 have deesclated the value to the date of preliminary notification.
This he has not done so.
He has not complied with the statutory provisions of 3G (7)(a) of National Highways Authority Act.

Therefore,
the award is patently illegal.
.20. The Arbitrator has relied upon guidelines value 07.10.2005.
This document is not valid record received from the Arbitrator as none of the parties have produced and this is evident from the record of the Arbitrator.
Section 24(3) of the Act provides provision regarding hearing and written proceedings.

It reads thus:
A.P. No.35/2020 "All statements, documents or other information supplied to, or applications made to the aribral tribunal by one party shall be communicated to the other party, and any expert report or evidentiary document on which the arbital tribunal may rely in making its decision shall be communicated to the parties".
.21.

As an Arbitrator has relied on the estimated guidelines value of immovable properties and buildings dated 07.10.2005 without bringing to the knowledge of the parties and thereby has failed to follow the procedure under Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
So the award has to be set aside on the ground of patent illegality.

.22. The petitioner has contended that the respondent No.2 has not assigned any reasons for re- determining the compensation; that he has not assigned any reasons for enhancing the compensation or for relying upon notification dated 07.10.2005.
.23.

Section 3(G) of the National High Ways Act, mandatorily provides that, the competent authority or the Arbitrator to take into consideration the factors A.P.
No.35/2020 mentioned in Sub clause (a) to (d) while determining the market value of the compensation payable in-respect of the acquired lands.
But neither the award nor the order sheet shows any materials on record as to how he had followed the said provision.

.24. In Som Dutt Builders Ltd Vs. State of Kerala (2010)2 AWC (supp) 1390 SC) has held that:
"Reasons must be indicated in the award as that would reflect thought process leading to a particular conclusion.

entities.text: Som Dutt Builders Ltd Vs. State of Kerala (2010)2 AWC (supp) 1390 SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To satisfy the requirement of Section 31(3), the reasons must be stated by the Arbitral Tribunal upon which the award is based; want of reasons would make such award legally flawed."

.25. On perusal of the records and the award of the Arbitrator it is seen that the respondent No.2 has neither complied with the procedure provided under Section 24 nor decided the dispute in accordance with Section 28(1)(a) and at the same time has failed to comply with Section 31(3) of the A.P./35/2020 on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168729828/
7 A & C Act, thus rendering the impugned Arbitral Award opposed to settled position of law.

. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd. Vs. SAW Piles Ltd., (AIR 2003 SC 2629) has held that:
"if the award is patently against the statutory provisions of Substantive law which is in force in India or is passed without giving an opportunity of hearing to the parties as provided under Section 24 or without giving any reason in a case where parties have not agreed that no reasons are to be recorded, it would be against the statutory provisions.

entities.text: Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd. Vs. SAW Piles Ltd., (AIR 2003 SC 2629)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In all such cases, the award is required to be set aside on the ground of 'patent illegality'
The above decision is applies to the case in hand.
In view of the above discussion, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative.
.27. Point No.2:

In view of the aforesaid finding on point No.1 I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER A.P. No.35/2020 is allowed.

The impugned award passed by the respondent No.2 in so far as pertaining to case No.LAQ/ARB/NH- A.P. No.35/2020 7/134/2012-13 pertaining to Sy.No.29/3 acquired to an extent of 2904 sq. feet is set aside.
(Dictated to the Judgment Writer, transcribed by her, revised by me and after corrections, pronounced in open Court on this the 18 th day of January 2023.)
(Sheila B.M.) II Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, & Spl. Judge, Bangalore.
